Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From the TV series Star Trek.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈkliŋːon/, [ˈkliŋːo̞n]
  • Rhymes: -iŋːon
  • Syllabification(key): klin‧gon
  • Hyphenation(key): klin‧gon

Noun

[edit]

klingon

  1. Klingon, Klingonese (fictional language)
  2. A Klingon (member of a fictional alien race)

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
klingon
Wikipedia fr

Etymology

[edit]

From the TV series Star Trek.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kliŋ.ɡɔn/, /klɛ̃.ɡɔ̃/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

klingon m (uncountable)

  1. the Klingon language

Adjective

[edit]

klingon (feminine klingonne, masculine plural klingons, feminine plural klingonnes)

  1. Klingon

Portuguese

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

klingon m (uncountable)

  1. Klingon (artificial language from the Star Trek franchise)

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From English Klingon, from Klingon tlhIngan.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈklinɡon/ [ˈklĩŋ.ɡõn]
  • Rhymes: -inɡon
  • Syllabification: klin‧gon

Adjective

[edit]

klingon (invariable)

  1. Klingon

Noun

[edit]

klingon m (plural klingon)

  1. (science fiction) Klingon (a member of the Klingon species in Star Trek)
  2. (science fiction) Klingon (artificial language from the Star Trek franchise)
    • 2019 February 17, Francisco Martínez Hoyos, “10 idiomas que se crearon de la nada”, in La Vanguardia‎[2], archived from the original on 2 August 2025:
      El klingon es el idioma que inventó en 1967 el lingüista Marc Okrand para un pueblo de guerreros humanoides en Star Trek, la popular saga de ciencia ficción.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
